subject: general
question: Since 2008, the United Nations is running a program REDD to create awareness for the importance of carbon stored in the forests, reduction of carbon emissions and investment in low carbon development. What does REDD stand for?

options.text: Recycling Energy from Deforestation and Forest Degradation
Renewable Energy from Disintegration and Forest Degradation
Reducing Emissions from Disintegration and Forest Degradation
Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation

solution:
The correct answer is __**Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD)** is a program initiated by the United Nations in 2008.
 
• The primary aim of REDD is to create awareness about the importance of carbon stored in forests and to reduce carbon emissions through conservation efforts.
 
• REDD also focuses on promoting investment in low carbon development and sustainable forest management.
 
• The program seeks to provide financial incentives to developing countries to reduce deforestation and forest degradation, thereby contributing to global climate change mitigation efforts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deforestation** refers to the large-scale removal of forest, leading to loss of biodiversity and disruption of ecosystems.
 
• **Forest degradation** involves the reduction in the capacity of a forest to provide goods and services, often due to logging, fire, or other disturbances.
 
• The REDD program is part of broader efforts under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) to address climate change and promote sustainable development.
 
• REDD+ is an extension of REDD, which includes the role of conservation, sustainable management of forests, and enhancement of forest carbon stocks.
